newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says confident of hitting RPIX target.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says confident of hitting RPIX target.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Wednesday that he was confident of hitting his 2.5 percent target for underlying inflation. "My target is 2.5 percent. I've always said I will set policy to achieve that target and I'm confident that we will get to that target," Clarke said on BBC radio.
Underlying inflation, excluding mortgage interest payments, edged up to 2.9 percent in September.
"I won't hesitate to take whatever measures are necessary to get there," Clarke said.

"It is important as this recovery accelerates that I stick to my 2.5 percent target. I never speculate about what I would do, I never tell people I will put interest rates up, down or keep them the same but...that 2.5 percent inflation target is a key part of policy-making."
Clarke meets Bank of England Governor Eddie George for their monthly discussion of monetary policy later on Wednesday.
At recent monetary meetings, George has called for base rates to be put up to 6.00 percent, from 5.75.
But with elections approaching by May 1997, Clarke is not expected to give way.
Clarke reiterated his pledge to cut public borrowing in such a way that it moves towards balance in the medium-term.
